why:
Measured against the recorded upstream surfaces (`docs/reference/api-surface/{rclc,rclcpp,rclrs}.json`): none of them contains `release`, `jitter` or `skip` on an executor, so there is no upstream name to align to. Same basis as the `Executor::release_jitter` pair beside it.

phase-474 I11. A periodic `spin_once(timeout)` with no declared cadence is released on an absolute grid (period = timeout). A loop that comes back a whole period or more after its next grid point is released once, for the latest due point; the older points are dropped, never released back to back, and this counts them. rclcpp has no counterpart because it does not own the release (see `Executor::release_jitter`). Paired with the jitter reading so a caller can tell a late release from a lost one.
